bull: Extremely oversold (RSI 22.7, -47% from 52w high) with a large valuation reset already priced in.
Adjusted revenue still grew 2% with 10bp of EBITDA margin expansion despite the tough environment.
bear: Full-year outlook was just lowered on weaker China/global auto production schedules.
Price is deeply below both SMA50 (-24%) and SMA200 (-33%) with no confirmed trend reversal yet.
APTV.summary: Aptiv crashed on a guidance cut tied to weak auto production and is now deeply oversold with no confirmed bottom.
APTV.key_risk: Continued China auto-production weakness extends the guidance cuts and delays any reversal.

bull: International Omnipod outlook was raised alongside strong overall revenue growth.
RSI 28 is oversold, leaving room for a technical bounce.
bear: A relatively small guidance cut triggered a 20% single-day crash, signaling the market sees a real U.S. competitive/growth problem.
Momentum divergence is negative (-6.5), meaning the selloff is accelerating, not stabilizing.
PODD.summary: Insulet's guidance trim exposed deeper concerns about U.S. Omnipod competitive positioning, and the selloff shows no sign of stabilizing yet.
PODD.key_risk: U.S. Type 2 onboarding execution issues worsen and further erode the growth narrative.

bull: Beat Q2 earnings/revenue with a strong Q3 outlook, driven by DTC strength and a Studios turnaround.
Stock is recovering (+10% 5d) off a depressed base, -57% from 52w high.
bear: Warner Bros. Discovery merger antitrust trial won't start until March 2027, exposing Paramount to over $1B/year in penalty accrual before any ruling.
Legacy TV Media revenue continues to decline, offsetting DTC gains.
PSKY.summary: Paramount Skydance beat and guided Q3 higher, but a multi-year merger litigation overhang with steep daily penalties caps the upside case.
PSKY.key_risk: The antitrust trial drags on with mounting penalty accrual, overwhelming the operational improvement.

bull: Guidance was held despite the selloff, with clinical-led volume/mortality-driven growth continuing.
RSI 20.9 is deeply oversold and the stock remains well above its SMA200 (+19%), suggesting the longer trend is intact.
bear: Margins narrowed on a weaker commercial payer mix, which is the core profitability lever for dialysis providers.
Reimbursement-rate pressure is an ongoing structural risk for the business.
DVA.summary: DaVita sold off hard despite an earnings beat because margins narrowed on payer mix, though management held full-year guidance.
DVA.key_risk: Commercial mix keeps deteriorating, compressing margins further even as volumes grow.

bull: Record Q2 with 20% sales growth and raised both Q3 and full-year guidance.
Analysts still see a ~13% fair-value gap even after the rally.
bear: RSI 89.2 and Bollinger position 120% (above the upper band) mark the stock as extremely overbought after a 30% five-day spike.
Momentum divergence is negative (-9.2), warning the rally's underlying strength is fading even as price stays elevated.
ZBRA.summary: Zebra posted a genuine record-beat-and-raise quarter, but the stock is technically extended after a 30% five-day spike and due for consolidation.
ZBRA.key_risk: A mean-reversion pullback from extremely overbought levels erases a chunk of the post-earnings gain.

bull: Commercial segment continues to post gains, partially offsetting residential weakness.
RSI 23.2 is oversold with positive momentum divergence (+20.8), hinting at a possible bottoming process.
bear: 2026 EPS guidance was cut on residential HVAC weakness, driving the -22% drop.
Still trading -14% below SMA50 with no confirmed reversal.
LII.summary: Lennox cut EPS guidance on residential softness and dropped sharply, though commercial strength and early bottoming signs offer some support.
LII.key_risk: Residential HVAC demand stays weak for longer than management currently expects.

bull: Multiple analyst upgrades on accelerating AI data-center demand with a potential doubling of that business.
Still trading above its SMA200 (+2%) despite the pullback, indicating the longer-term uptrend is intact.
bear: Short-term momentum remains negative (MACD -5.9, RSI 35) and semis are a highly cyclical, volatile group.
Stock is still -43% from its 52-week high, showing the prior drawdown was severe.
ON.summary: ON Semiconductor has pulled back sharply but analysts are turning more positive on its AI data-center exposure, with the long-term trend still intact.
ON.key_risk: Broader semiconductor cyclicality or an AI capex slowdown undercuts the data-center growth thesis.

bull: Q2 beat on both bookings and profit, showing the core business remains healthy.
Robotaxi push gives an additional long-term growth lever beyond core ride-hailing.
bear: Forward bookings guidance disappointed, which is what actually drove the selloff.
Trading below both SMA50 (-4.9%) and SMA200 (-12.8%) with volume 2.6x average on the drop.
UBER.summary: Uber beat on the current quarter but a soft bookings guide overshadowed results, with the robotaxi transition adding both opportunity and cost uncertainty.
UBER.key_risk: Bookings growth continues to decelerate as robotaxi investment weighs on near-term profitability.

bull: Raised full-year revenue guidance to $16.05-16.22B on strong travel demand.
Only -2.2% from its 52-week high, confirming a healthy underlying uptrend.
bear: RSI 74.8 and Bollinger position 105% (above upper band) show the stock is technically overbought after a 23% 20-day run.
Momentum divergence is sharply negative (-17.7), a classic warning that the rally is losing steam.
EXPE.summary: Expedia raised guidance on strong travel demand, but the stock is technically overextended after a 20-day run and momentum is already decelerating.
EXPE.key_risk: A pullback from overbought levels gives back a meaningful chunk of the recent rally before guidance strength can reassert.

bull: Book-to-bill ratio hit a four-year high (1.19x), signaling a genuine demand inflection in preclinical/CRO research.
Beat Q2 targets with margin improvement from portfolio refinements.
bear: RSI 69.3 and Bollinger position 135% show the stock is now technically extended after an 11% single-day pop.
Momentum divergence is negative (-5.4), suggesting some near-term consolidation risk after the spike.
CRL.summary: Charles River's four-year-high book-to-bill signals a real demand recovery in contract research, even though the stock is technically stretched right after the pop.
CRL.key_risk: Biotech/pharma R&D budget pressure resumes and the book-to-bill improvement proves temporary.

bull: Data-center and manufacturing demand is driving robust customer and sales growth for the utility.
RSI 22.1 oversold on light volume (0.73x) suggests a slow drift down rather than a panic selloff — a defensive, lower-risk setup.
bear: EPS fell $0.15 YoY on higher interest expense and depreciation, a headwind that persists as capex ramps for data-center demand.
Regulated-utility rate case outcomes remain a swing factor for earnings.
PNW.summary: Pinnacle West is a low-drama scout candidate riding data-center-driven demand growth, offset by rising financing costs pressuring near-term EPS.
PNW.key_risk: Higher-for-longer interest rates keep pressuring EPS faster than rate-base growth can offset it.

bull: Operating EBITDA grew 9.1% excluding one-off wildfire cleanup contributions, a genuinely strong underlying result.
Recognized as a low-volatility, reliable dividend-growth defensive name.
bear: Management trimmed the sales forecast even as profitability held up, raising questions about top-line durability.
RSI 22.4 oversold but on largely flat SMA trend — no clear bottoming catalyst yet.
WM.summary: Waste Management delivered strong underlying EBITDA growth but trimmed its sales forecast, leaving a defensive but growth-questioned setup.
WM.key_risk: Volume/pricing softness that drove the trimmed sales forecast persists and pressures the growth narrative further.

bull: High occupancy and steady rent growth position Realty Income for a potential earnings-season positive surprise per multiple sources.
Active investment activity continues to support the growth pipeline.
bear: As a REIT, it remains sensitive to higher borrowing costs, which continue to pressure the group.
RSI 22.6 oversold reflects broader rate-driven REIT weakness rather than a company-specific catalyst.
O.summary: Realty Income screens as a scout candidate ahead of Q2 earnings, with multiple sources flagging positive-surprise potential despite rate-driven REIT weakness.
O.key_risk: Borrowing costs stay elevated for longer, continuing to weigh on REIT valuations broadly regardless of operating performance.

bull: Strong 20% five-day rally with a bullish Street view (one CIO sees S&P 500 climbing to $8,000 partly on names like Amazon).
RSI 61.7 and positive MACD show healthy, not yet extreme, momentum.
bear: -1.7% today shows some profit-taking after the sharp rally.
AI capex/competitive dynamics among Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet remain a swing factor for sentiment.
AMZN.summary: Amazon, a current holding, is riding strong momentum on broad AI/cloud optimism with technicals still healthy rather than overextended.
AMZN.key_risk: A rotation out of mega-cap AI winners on capex or margin concerns interrupts the current rally.

bull: AI-driven contract manufacturing demand (mirrored by peer Jabil's 31.6% six-month surge) is lifting the whole group, and analysts remain bullish on Flex specifically.
Momentum divergence is strongly positive (+26.9), confirming the rally has real underlying strength.
bear: Still -12% below its SMA50 despite the +18% five-day rally, showing high realized volatility.
Volume ratio is below average (0.56x), so the move lacks strong volume confirmation.
FLEX.summary: Flex, a current holding, is benefiting from the same AI-manufacturing tailwind lifting peers like Jabil, with strong momentum confirming the move.
FLEX.key_risk: AI-related capex growth slows and the contract-manufacturing tailwind fades faster than expected.

bull: Momentum divergence is strongly positive (+41.2), the strongest reading in the deep set, suggesting building underlying strength.
Potential tariffs/price floors on imported polysilicon could favor domestic optical/glass supply chains Corning participates in.
bear: Still -13% below SMA50 despite the recent rally, reflecting high realized volatility.
No direct company-specific catalyst in recent headlines — the move looks more sector/momentum-driven than fundamentals-driven.
GLW.summary: Corning, a current holding, shows the strongest momentum divergence in the set but lacks a clear company-specific news catalyst behind the recent rally.
GLW.key_risk: The rally proves to be indiscriminate sector rotation rather than company-specific strength, and gives back gains on the next pullback.

bull: Outperformed the broader market over the past year with Wall Street maintaining a cautiously optimistic view.
Steady uptrend with price near its 52-week high (-1.5%).
bear: RSI 74.9 and Bollinger position 84% show the stock is overbought after a strong run.
An insider (Kevin H. Rhodes) exercised options and immediately sold in the open market, and momentum divergence is negative (-15.4), both cautionary signals.
MMM.summary: 3M's steady uptrend looks stretched here, with overbought technicals, fading momentum divergence, and a notable insider sale all pointing to near-term caution.
MMM.key_risk: A technical pullback from overbought levels is compounded by the insider-selling signal, pressuring the stock despite the longer-term uptrend.

bull: AI networking/communications demand is accelerating and being cited as a key driver of the renewed semiconductor rally.
Momentum divergence is strongly positive (+38.1), confirming real strength behind the +29% five-day move.
bear: Still -36% from its 52-week high, reflecting a severe prior drawdown that hasn't fully reversed.
Margin pressure from uneven segment mix remains an execution risk even as communications recovers.
MRVL.summary: Marvell, a current holding, is riding an accelerating AI-networking recovery with strong confirmed momentum, though it remains well off its highs and margin execution is still a risk.
MRVL.key_risk: Margin pressure from mix persists and offsets the top-line benefit of the communications-segment recovery.

bull: Diversified, recurring-revenue fintech/data business with a new Verafin-D-Wave partnership adding a quantum-computing financial-crime-detection angle.
Broader tech sector strength is providing a supportive backdrop.
bear: Lowest screener score in the deep set (8.5), indicating weak momentum signal relative to peers.
Price action is essentially flat over 5 days (-1%) with no clear catalyst.
NDAQ.summary: Nasdaq Inc, a current holding, is a steady diversified fintech name with a minor positive partnership headline but no strong momentum signal right now.
NDAQ.key_risk: Trading/listing revenue softens if market volatility and volumes cool from current elevated levels.

bull: Subscription growth and AI monetization remain strong per management, and some prominent analysts (Dan Ives) remain bullish despite the sell-off.
A Q2 2026 investor letter flagged it as a potentially mispriced AI winner after the software sell-off.
bear: Down 23% YTD on AI-competition and valuation concerns that haven't fully resolved.
Momentum divergence is negative (-7.5), suggesting the recent bounce (+8.8% 20d) may be losing steam.
NOW.summary: ServiceNow, a current holding, remains down sharply YTD on AI-competition fears, but subscription fundamentals and some high-profile bullish calls argue it may be mispriced to the downside.
NOW.key_risk: AI-native competitors continue eroding ServiceNow's workflow-automation moat faster than subscription growth can compensate.

bull: Earnings surged with a 77% increase in EPS last year and a 213th consecutive dividend declared, underscoring a genuine turnaround.
Price is near its 52-week high (-1.9%), confirming a strong uptrend.
bear: RSI 77.9 and Bollinger position 98% mark the stock as very overbought after the run.
Momentum divergence is negative (-13.9), a clear warning the rally is decelerating even as price sits near highs.
NUE.summary: Nucor's earnings turnaround is real and the dividend streak intact, but the stock is very overbought near its 52-week high with fading momentum underneath.
NUE.key_risk: A mean-reversion pullback from very overbought levels interrupts the run despite solid underlying earnings improvement.

bull: Reported strong fiscal Q3 results, and the aerospace-aftermarket business retains a durable competitive moat.
Relatively low realized volatility (RSI 54, near both SMAs) versus the rest of the deep set.
bear: Stock declined despite beating results, with investors specifically focused on margin trajectory and M&A pricing discipline going forward.
-14% from its 52-week high shows some loss of investor confidence even amid strong reported numbers.
TDG.summary: TransDigm beat Q3 estimates but investors are more focused on forward margins and M&A discipline than the current beat, capping the immediate reaction.
TDG.key_risk: Margin trajectory disappoints or an M&A deal is priced in a way investors view as value-destructive.

bull: Raised its 2026 revenue outlook on CF franchise growth, newer products, and a near-term renal launch, with UBS and RBC both reiterating positive views ahead of pipeline catalysts.
Diversification beyond cystic fibrosis reduces single-franchise concentration risk.
bear: Q2 EPS missed estimates even as revenue beat, a mixed signal worth watching.
Biotech pipeline catalysts carry binary trial/regulatory risk.
VRTX.summary: Vertex, a current holding, raised its revenue outlook on diversification beyond CF and has sell-side support heading into pipeline catalysts, despite a mixed EPS print.
VRTX.key_risk: An upcoming pipeline catalyst (trial or regulatory readout) disappoints, given the binary nature of biotech events.
